root_cause.text: The RedBoot MTD partition parser compared dynamically allocated partition-name strings with fixed-length memcmp() calls, so when names pointed to the end of a strlen-sized allocation, longer comparison lengths could read past the allocated buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch in drivers/mtd/parsers/redboot.c replaces `memcmp(names, ..., 8/15/14)` with `strcmp(names, ...)`, and the commit message explicitly states that "`names` is pointing to the final `namelen` many bytes of the allocation" and that the fortify warning was a legitimate "buffer overflow" caused by reading beyond the end of the allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use exact string matching for RedBoot partition names so only the intended reserved partitions are marked read-only.
intent_record.what: The change replaces three fixed-length string comparisons using memcmp() with exact null-terminated string comparisons using strcmp() for the partition names "RedBoot", "RedBoot config", and "FIS directory" inside the CONFIG_MTD_REDBOOT_PARTS_READONLY conditional.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the read-only flag is now applied only when the partition name exactly matches one of those three reserved names, instead of matching any name that merely shares the same leading bytes for the specified lengths. This prevents unintended partitions with matching prefixes from being marked non-writeable.

grouping_result.intent: Use exact string matching for RedBoot partition names so only the intended reserved partitions are marked read-only.

relevance_review.reason: The change replaces fixed-length partition-name comparisons with exact string matching in the RedBoot parser, directly addressing the unsafe memcmp()-style over-read on dynamically allocated name buffers described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This fixed-length memcmp reads 8 bytes from a dynamically allocated string buffer sized to strlen(name)+1. If the actual name is shorter and stored at the end of the allocation, comparing 8 bytes can read past the allocated buffer.
This comparison uses a hard-coded length of 15 against a dynamically allocated partition name string. If names points to a shorter allocation, memcmp may access bytes beyond the end of the buffer.
This fixed-size memcmp can over-read the allocated name buffer when the partition name is shorter than 14 bytes, matching the root cause of out-of-bounds reads on dynamically allocated strings.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs a fixed-length memcmp of 8 bytes against a dynamically allocated partition-name string. If the allocated string is shorter and positioned at the end of its allocation, the comparison can read past the buffer.
This statement compares 15 bytes from the dynamically allocated names buffer regardless of its actual string length, causing a potential out-of-bounds read when the partition name is shorter.
This statement uses a fixed-length 14-byte memcmp on the dynamically allocated partition-name string, which can over-read beyond the allocated buffer when the actual name is shorter.
